audit_findings.title: Gross cash bridge may include funds owed to promoters
audit_findings.magnitude: $189.285m, equal to $3.84 per diluted share and 14.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: Amounts collected in advance of events for which the Company is not the promoter or co-promoter do not represent contract liabilities and are recorded in Accounts payable, accrued and other current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge problem: the valuation adds the entire $293.599m cash balance, while the filed balance sheet records $189.285m of cash due to promoters as a current liability. Treating promoter settlement funds as surplus equity cash could materially inflate the valuation, although the exact adjustment still requires tracing the cash and working-capital accounts.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile promoter collections to cash and event settlements, determine the minimum operating-cash requirement, and rerun all scenarios using only distributable excess cash net of the associated claims.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may include material non-cash arena-license revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.694m of FY2026 non-cash revenue, equal to 30.8% of the $73.6m OE anchor; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Arena license fees include operating lease revenue of (i) $45,374 and $44,052 collected in cash for Fiscal Year 2026 and 2025 , respectively, and (ii) a non-cash portion of $22,694 and $24,016 for Fiscal Year 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that a material portion of arena-license revenue was non-cash, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation already removed it through an explicit adjustment or the change in the unbilled lease receivable. If retained in OE, the anchor materially exceeds current cash receipts.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2026 OE reconciliation from net income through working-capital adjustments, verify treatment of the unbilled lease receivable, and rerun the DCF if the $22.694m non-cash component was retained.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ruling conflicts with a contemplated theater transfer
audit_findings.evidence: In June 2026, the Company announced that it had entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with Penn Transformation Partners, a consortium comprised of Halmar Infrastructure Development, Inc. and Skanska Infrastructure Development, Inc. (collectively, the “Master Developer”), contemplating the transfer of the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden to the Master Developer in connection with the redevelopment of Penn Station, subject to further negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, see “Item 1A. Risk Factors — Economic and Operational Risks — The redevelopment of Penn Station may disrupt the operations of The Garden, which may adversely affect our business and results of operations” for further details.
audit_findings.explanation: The MOU and potential disruption are disclosed facts, but the contemplated transfer remained non-binding and its consideration, taxes, theater earnings, transition costs and disruption effects are not supplied. The event therefore cannot presently be entered as a demonstrated valuation adjustment; it could reduce ongoing OE while adding disposal proceeds to the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the MOU and any subsequent definitive agreements, isolate the theater's OE and maintenance capital, estimate taxes and consideration, and rerun the perimeter and disruption cases when terms become measurable.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring may be recurring rather than safely removable
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.986m in FY2026 and $32.690m over FY2024-FY2026; FY2026 equals 19.0% of the $73.6m OE anchor
audit_findings.evidence: During Fiscal Year 2026, the Company recorded restructuring charges of $ 13,986 , inclusive of $ 56 of share-based compensation benefits, primarily related to termination benefits provided as part of a voluntary exit program.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates restructuring charges in all three disclosed years, but the record does not show whether the OE series added them back. If they were removed without a normalized recurring allowance, OE and the resulting valuation could be materially overstated. The existence of an error remains conditional on the missing OE reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each year's OE adjustments, identify cash restructuring and severance payments, establish a normalized recurring allowance from filed history and management evidence, and rerun all scenarios if any unsupported add-back was made.

audit_findings.title: The investment bridge appears to include assets owed to employees
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $6.923m, equal to $0.14 per diluted share and 0.52% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: In accordance with ASC Topic 710, the Company remeasures the deferred compensation liability, with a charge (or credit) to compensation cost in the consolidated statements of operations, to reflect changes in the fair value of the assets owed to the participants of the Deferred Compensation Plan.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated classification error: $6.924m of trust investments is matched by approximately $6.923m of deferred-compensation liabilities and is not an incremental common-equity asset. The resulting approximately $0.14-per-share overstatement is too small relative to the $27.10 base value, $77.41 market price and 30% margin-of-safety threshold to change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Offset the trust assets with the matching liability, retain only approximately $1.855m of unencumbered investments, and update the bridge and per-share outputs.

audit_findings.title: The valuation does not expose the $45 million property-tax exemption risk
audit_findings.magnitude: $45m FY2026 exemption; MSGE license-fee exposure unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: For Fiscal Year 2026, the tax exemption was $45 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $45m exemption and political challenge are filed facts, but MSG Sports bears the property tax and the record does not provide the contractual percentage reduction in fees payable to MSGE. No repeal is shown as effective at the valuation date, so this is a forward-looking risk rather than a demonstrated error in current OE; realization would reduce future license-fee cash flows.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Arena License Agreements' tax-adjustment formulas, track repeal legislation and the 2028 permit process, quantify MSGE's fee reduction under partial and full repeal, and rerun probability-weighted bear and base cases when measurable.
